newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - French vol on hold ahead of German data.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - French vol on hold ahead of German data.

text.p: The prospect of German unemployment data later in the week is preventing a slide in French interest rate options volatility, traders said on Tuesday.

The data, due for release on Thursday, are expected to provide a clear insight into the strength of the German economy, and also add more fuel to the debate over the likelihood of a delay to European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).
"Short-term, the unemployment figures are keeping the vol up," said a trader at a French brokerage in Paris. "After that, I'd expect to see vol coming off across the board."
However, he said while talk of a delay to EMU was still circulating in the market, it would prevent a major fall in the levels, which were drifting off gradually.
"That should put a floor under it," he said. "Volatility is pretty fairly valued given the increasing concerns over EMU, which surfaced last week."

Implied volatility for March PIBOR options was at 14 percent, slightly off from 14.4 at the previous close. June fell back 18 percent from 18.8 percent, September was at 19.5 percent from 19.6 percent.
March PIBOR futures were up one basis point at 96.64 by 1330 GMT, while June was up two basis points also at 96.64.
A trader at a French bank in Paris said there would be a sell-off towards the end of the week in volatility, as the market was also awaiting the U.S. non-farm payrolls report.

In options on notionnel futures, volatility was also marginally weaker across the series, traders said. April options on the June notionnel future fell to 4.7 percent, from 4.8 percent, while May fell 4.7 percent from 4.75.
June and September were flat at 4.85 percent.
The June notionnel future was trading at 132.18 at 1350 GMT, up 20 basis points on Tuesday's close.
In PIBOR options, activity was clustered around the June puts at the 96.40, 96.50, 96.60 strikes and in the 96.60 and 96.70 strike calls.
